ant — Claude Platform CLI

 
 

 ant is the official CLI for the Claude Platform. It puts the Claude API in your terminal — send messages, manage agents and sessions, upload files, and script against every API endpoint.

 

 Documentation

Full documentation is available at platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/sdks/cli .

 Installation

 

 Installing with Homebrew

 

 Installing with Go

To test or install the CLI locally, you need Go version 1.22 or later installed.

 

Once you have run go install , the binary is placed in your Go bin directory:

- Default location : $HOME/go/bin (or $GOPATH/bin if GOPATH is set)
- Check your path : Run go env GOPATH to see the base directory

If commands aren't found after installation, add the Go bin directory to your PATH:

 

 

 Getting started

Log in with your Claude Console account:

 

Or set the ANTHROPIC API KEY environment variable to an API key from the Claude Console.

To hand the CLI a key from a secret manager without putting it in the environment, pipe it on stdin:

 

Then send your first message:

 

Structured flags accept relaxed JSON or YAML, so unquoted keys are fine.

 Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed)

Sign in with Google and name your workspace; the CLI then sends requests through the Google Cloud gateway and keeps the Google access token fresh:

 

The same settings are available as --google-cloud-project , --google-cloud-workspace-id and --google-cloud-location (default global ). The project defaults to the one your Google credentials carry. Any credentials Google's Application Default Credentials find are used, including a service account key named by GOOGLE APPLICATION CREDENTIALS . An API key, an auth token or a profile named with --profile takes precedence; ant auth status shows which is in use. Google credentials are sent only to the gateway: --base-url and ANTHROPIC BASE URL are not used, and --google-cloud-base-url ( ANTHROPIC GOOGLE CLOUD BASE URL ) overrides the gateway URL. ant beta:worker is not supported on Google Cloud.

 Claude Platform on AWS

Name your region and workspace; the CLI then sends requests through the Claude Platform on AWS gateway, signed with your AWS credentials:

 

The same settings are available as --aws-region and --aws-workspace-id . Either flag, ANTHROPIC AWS WORKSPACE ID or an AWS API key selects AWS; AWS REGION and AWS PROFILE on their own don't, since most AWS machines set them for other reasons. The region defaults to AWS REGION , then AWS DEFAULT REGION . Any credentials the AWS default credential chain finds are used, including AWS PROFILE , environment keys and an IAM role. To use an API key generated in the AWS Console instead, set ANTHROPIC AWS API KEY or pipe it to --aws-api-key-stdin . The key works only in the region it was generated in, so set the region to match. ANTHROPIC API KEY , an auth token, a profile named with --profile or Google Cloud settings take precedence; ant auth status shows which is in use. AWS credentials are sent only to the gateway: --base-url and ANTHROPIC BASE URL are not used, and --aws-base-url ( ANTHROPIC AWS BASE URL ) overrides the gateway URL. ant beta:worker is not supported on AWS.

 Claude in Microsoft Foundry

Name your resource and set an API key from the Foundry portal. The CLI then sends requests to that resource:

 

 --model takes the name of your deployment, which defaults to the model ID. To use Microsoft Entra ID instead of an API key, set an access token:

 

The CLI doesn't refresh the token, so set it again when it expires.

 --foundry-resource also sets the resource, and --foundry-api-key-stdin and --foundry-auth-token-stdin read the key or the token from standard input. A key, a token or --foundry-resource selects Foundry; ANTHROPIC FOUNDRY RESOURCE on its own doesn't, since a Claude Code setup can export it with no key or token. When both a key and a token are set, the piped one is used; when both come from the environment, the token is used, as in Claude Code, and the CLI prints a note. ANTHROPIC API KEY , an auth token, a profile named with --profile , Google Cloud settings and AWS settings take precedence, and ant auth status shows which is in use. Foundry credentials are sent only to your resource, so --base-url and ANTHROPIC BASE URL are not used. ANTHROPIC CUSTOM HEADERS is not applied either. To send requests to another URL, set --foundry-base-url ( ANTHROPIC FOUNDRY BASE URL ) in place of the resource, and include the /anthropic path. Claude in Microsoft Foundry lists the features available there. ant beta:worker is not supported on Foundry.

 Requirements

macOS, Linux, or Windows.

 Contributing

See CONTRIBUTING.md. The sandboxes/ directory, the pieces for running Claude Managed Agents self-hosted sandboxes, is a separate Go module with its own README.

install.title: Installation
install.html:
Installing with Homebrew
brew install anthropics/tap/ant
Installing with Go

To test or install the CLI locally, you need Go version 1.22 or later installed.

go install 'github.com/anthropics/anthropic-cli/v2/cmd/ant@latest'

Once you have run go install, the binary is placed in your Go bin directory:

  • Default location: $HOME/go/bin (or $GOPATH/bin if GOPATH is set)
  • Check your path: Run go env GOPATH to see the base directory

If commands aren't found after installation, add the Go bin directory to your PATH:

# Add to your shell profile (.zshrc, .bashrc, etc.)
export PATH="$PATH:$(go env GOPATH)/bin"
